subcommands.name: clip
subcommands.description: Creates a bookmark for the specified file or URL and copies its Hookmark URL to the clipboard. The copied Hookmark URL can be used to link to other files (use `hook link --paste FILE/URL`, or to paste into another app as a link. Use the -m flag to copy a full Markdown link.

subcommands.name: link
subcommands.description: If two files/urls are provided, links will be bi-directional. If three or more are provided, `link` defaults to creating bi-directional links between each file and the last file in the list. Use `-a` to create bi-directional links between every file in the list. If using `--paste`, the URL/hook link in the clipboard will be used as one argument, to be combined with one or more file/url arguments.

options.description: Link every listed file or url to every other

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.description: Output a list of all hooks attached to given url(s) or file(s) in the specified format (default "paths"). Run `hook list` with no file/url argument to list all bookmarks.

options.description: Output only bookmarks with file paths (exclude e.g. emails)
Separate results with NULL separator, only applies with "paths" output for single file argument
Generate a menu to select hook(s) for opening

subcommands.name: find
subcommands.description: Search bookmark urls and names for a string and output in specified format (default "paths"). Run `hook find` with no search argument to list all bookmarks.

options.description: Output only bookmarks with file paths (exclude e.g. emails)
Separate results with NULL separator, only applies with "paths" output for single file argument

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.description: Remove a hook between two files or URLs. If you use --all, all hooks on a given file will be removed. If --all isn't specified, exactly two arguments (Files/URLs) are required.

options.description: Remove ALL links on files, requires confirmation

subcommands.name: clone
subcommands.description: Copy all the files and urls that the first file is hooked to onto another file. Exactly two arguments (SOURCE, TARGET) required.

subcommands.name: from
subcommands.description: Specify an application by name (without '.app') to bring that app to the foreground and create a bookmark for the active document, note, task, etc., returning a Hookmark URL. Use -m to get the response as Markdown, and/or -c to copy the result directly to the clipboard.
